messages:
OpsBot: ALERT: throttle-events high on rw-inference-prod-usw2. signal=throttle_rate tokens/sec spike > 3x baseline, queue_depth > 120, 502s beginning at ~2112233400. paging oncall_rotation (severity=P2)
Samir Patel: I see it, getting paged. Confirming customer-facing errors?
OpsBot: Some routes reporting 502/504 from backend inference workers, user-facing error rate ~0.6% of requests across routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat (metrics link: https://telemetry.redwood/alerts/2112233445)
Lee Johnson: @Samir can you grab capacity dashboard and check Dedicated pool saturation?
Samir Patel: On it. Quick check: gpux-dedicated-usw2 utilization 98% on L0, pending queue per-node ~45, autoscaler hasn't reacted fast enough because scale_cooldown=120s.
Maria Gomez: We're also seeing a tokens/sec spike correlated with a small subset of customers sending long streams. Might be a noisy tenant.
Jun Park: Any throttles leading to cascade? I want to see if throttles -> retries -> queueing loop.
Samir Patel: Logs show repeated retries from r-client-42 (customer A) at ~2112233387, pattern: immediate retry after 429. Example log: ```2026-03-12T21:23:40Z r-client-42 POST /v1/generate 429 retry=1````
Aisha Khan: If we're hitting 98% GPU, immediate mitigation options: 1) increase pool size (hot-path) 2) enable fallback model variant with lower mem/latency 3) apply per-tenant throttling/soft-qps to noisy tenant.
Lee Johnson: Can we spin a hot pool? Samir, what is lead time?
Samir Patel: I can request burst capacity from Dedicated (reserve-burst API) but it takes ~70s to attach. Command: `infra-cli dedicate attach --region usw2 --pool gpux-dedicated --size +4`
Samir Patel: Doing it now. `> infra-cli ...`
deploy-bot: canary rollback not triggered. No deploys in last 30m.
Maria Gomez: Meanwhile I'll add a temporary rate limit at the edge for the noisy tenant: `edgectl rate-limit set tenant=r-client-42 qps=4 window=60s`
Jun Park: Good. Also we should mute noisy alerts for queue_depth to avoid page storms while we fix. @Samir can you mute the specific alert ID?
Samir Patel: Muting alert `alerts/queue_depth_usw2_gpux_L0` for 15m. `> alertctl mute alerts/queue_depth_usw2_gpux_L0 --duration 15m`
Samir Patel: Burst attach started, ETA ~70s.
OpsBot: Update: Dedicated pool resize in progress (job 8779), expected attached in 65s.
Maria Gomez: Rate limit applied to r-client-42. Initial effect: tokens/sec for that tenant dropping by ~75% already.
Lee Johnson: Nice. Monitor for retries/backoff. Also activate fallback variant for high-req routes to reduce memory/latency per request. Aisha, can you flip traffic?
Aisha Khan: Flipping `/v1/generate` -> fallback-variant (quantized) for canary 10% now. `routectl set variant /v1/generate fallback-quantized --canary 10%`
Jun Park: Keep an eye on quality alerts. This is short-term mitigation only.
Samir Patel: Dedicated +4 attached. Pool utilization dropped to 74%, queue depth now trending down to 40. Throttles still occasional but user error rate dropping.
OpsBot: ALERT: throttle_rate decreased to 1.2x baseline. 502s dropping.
Lee Johnson: Good. Now the post-incident tuning discussion: we need to avoid paging for noisy spike that is handled by burst attach and edge rate limit. Proposals: raise queue_depth alert threshold, add a tokens/sec per-tenant hot-spot alert, and introduce alert debounce for 2 consecutive windows before paging.
Maria Gomez: +1. Concrete values suggestion: queue_depth_pager -> from 100 to 160 (or make it dynamic by cluster size), tokens/sec per-cluster pager if sustained > 2.5x baseline for 3m. Also add a new dashboard tile to show top 10 tenants by tokens/sec with auto-refresh.
Jun Park: Also we should add a circuit-breaker runbook step to auto-apply soft tenant caps for top N noisy tenants when tokens/sec >= threshold. That reduces blast radius and prevents cascade.
Aisha Khan: Action items: 1) Update alert rule: `alerts/queue_depth_usw2_gpux_L0` threshold->160 and add 3m debounce. 2) New alert `alerts/tokens_hotspot_tenant` for per-tenant sustained >2.5x baseline for 3m. 3) Dashboard `ops/inference/hot-tenants` showing top tenants, throttles, retries. 4) Runbook update to include `edgectl rate-limit` and `routectl` fallback variant steps.
Samir Patel: I'll file the follow-up ticket and queue config change in infra-alarms repo. Ticket: INF-5421 "Tune queue_depth paging + tenant hotspot alerts". Assign to eng-sre + eng-runtime.
Maria Gomez: I'll draft the dashboard tile and runbook snippet. Jun, can you review the circuit-breaker proposal?
Jun Park: Yup, will review. Also recommend adding a signal that correlates retries with queue_depth so alerts can be suppressed if retry storms cause transient spikes.
OpsBot: NOTE: paging for `alerts/queue_depth_usw2_gpux_L0` muted until 2112234345 per Samir.
deploy-bot: deploy noticed: infra/alerting updated (PR #2488) merged to staging. No code deploy to inference service.
Aisha Khan: Quick customer impact note for ops: Incident lasted ~12m from initial spike to mitigation fullness. Estimated affected requests ~0.6% with degraded responses and a tiny subset getting 502/504. No broad data loss.
Samir Patel: Marking thread resolved on-call handoff. Leaving postmortem draft in INF-5421. I'll also schedule a follow-up meeting to validate thresholds with product for customer latency tolerance.
Lee Johnson: Thanks team. Post-incident checklist: 1) confirm alert rule change in prod (Samir) 2) dashboard tile up (Maria) 3) runbook updated and tested (Jun) 4) customer outreach note if product wants (Aisha).
Maria Gomez: I'll upload a GIF to the ticket showing the tokens/sec spike -> rate-limit -> drop. :) :thumbsup:
Aisha Khan: Closing loop: any additional probs, re-open thread. Great job quick mitigation. :party_parrot:
